target.named_primary_source: SpaceMind: A Modular and Self-Evolving Embodied Vision-Language Agent Framework for Autonomous On-orbit Servicing

verified_primary_evidence.mutation_semantics: Paper method defines create, overlay, rewrite, disable, and no_change; disable is specifically described as disabling a learned skill found harmful. The mutation path is guarded by a quality gate including safety blacklist, fingerprint deduplication, task-scope binding, and parent-skill validation, with rejected mutations audited.
verified_primary_evidence.self_evolution_design: 30 runs arranged as 6 groups x 5 consecutive rounds, Standard mode with Hybrid-Nav.
verified_primary_evidence.detailed_outcomes: Four of six groups have positive/strong-positive study outcomes, but only two groups are explicit baseline FAIL cases: New Horizons Search C1 recovers to 3/5 and New Horizons Rendezvous C3 recovers to 5/5. The paper text says three of six groups show significant improvement by Round 1 or 2.
verified_primary_evidence.inspection_metric_scope: Huygens inspection starts at 12 points; Table 6 reports best=68, while text reports average across rounds=59.4. Thus the abstract shorthand 12-to-59 corresponds to the rounded average, not the best score.
verified_primary_evidence.physical_scope: Physical validation contains 18 runs on a myAGV Pro 3-DoF planar laboratory platform. Rendezvous is 6/6, search is 4/6, inspection average is 36.8, and one inspection collision is reported. The 100% physical result is rendezvous-only, not overall physical success or on-orbit validation.

official_code_observation.provenance_scope: Current public main is post-paper/expanded: README reports 363 closed-loop runs and a July 2026 Three.js environment, while arXiv v1 reports 192 closed-loop runs. README explicitly says Three.js is not for reproducing exact paper numbers. Current main therefore supports mechanism semantics but is not an exact tagged v1 reproduction snapshot.

scope_corrections: The abstract and current README say four of six groups recover from failure after a single failed episode, but the detailed experiment decomposes this as four positive groups, two explicit baseline-failure recoveries, and three groups with significant improvement by Round 1 or 2. Preserve that detailed decomposition instead of treating all four as one-episode failed-baseline recoveries.

The method supports revocable learned-skill state in principle, but the reported positive study cases do not isolate an actual rewrite/disable revocation as the cause of recovery. No matched ablation tests removing revocability.
This is not direct evidence that a false persistent scientific constraint can be revoked to reopen a previously excluded optimum. That stronger claim remains NOT_DIRECTLY_TESTED.
The 100% real-world figure is 6/6 rendezvous trials on the laboratory platform, not an overall physical success rate and not an on-orbit/6-DoF result.
